title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: (CXLD) Wine Confidence 101: Understanding the Basics
location: Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

This introductory course offers a comprehensive overview of essential wine concepts, designed to establish or strengthen your foundational knowledge and support your ongoing appreciation of wine. 

Over the 5-week course, we will review the primary grape varieties and styles of dry white, rosé, red, and sparkling wines, as well as explore viticulture fundamentals and the winemaking process. We will explore the major wine-producing countries and differences among grape varieties and wine styles. We will review how to taste and critically evaluate wine from visual assessment through aftertaste. For historical context, the course provides an overview of wine’s origins, its evolution, and the business aspects of winemaking. A solid foundation also includes guidance on appropriate tools for opening wine bottles, optimal storage, and serving temperatures to enhance your overall wine experience. 

By the end of the 5-week class, you will have gained a deeper understanding of the many aspects of dry and sparkling wines so you are thoroughly conversant about wine and have tasted between 20 – 25 different wines from around the world! 

THIS EVENT IS 21  Students will be required to show a government ID to the instructor upon arriving at the first session.

title: AI Basics in Gemini and Claude for Seasoned Professionals NEW
location: Montclair Bellevue Ave Branch - First Floor, Montclair Bellevue Avenue Branch
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Using AI as a thinking partner—not a replacement for expertise

Designed for experienced professionals who want to understand and responsibly integrate AI into their work, this 90-minute workshop introduces the core features of Google Gemini and Anthropic’s Claude. Participants will explore Gemini’s GEMs and image generation capabilities, as well as Claude’s artifacts and strengths in analyzing and generating longer-form content.

The session includes practical guidance on effective prompting frameworks, multimodal workflows, and the everyday language of AI. Real-world use cases will be discussed to help participants apply AI as a strategic collaborator while maintaining their own voice and expertise.

Participants should bring a laptop or tablet and be logged into the free versions of Gemini and Claude before class. Handouts will be provided.

title: Home Repair Essentials NEW
location: Montclair - Montclair High School, Montclair Public Library
description:

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, Robert will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

Nothing says The Twilight Zone like stories about enchanted objects, mystical forces or the presence of magic. title: Inspiration trap creativity workshop
description:
Live African music and drumming events in NJ
6,7&8pm Issyra Gallery presents - Inspiration Trap Creativity workshop

Only 10 attendees allowed social distancing and mandatory mask wearing.

You are invited to participate in a special session of creative thinking and fresh insight dedicated to inspiration.

We live in a world of constant change that requires us to be able to continually adapt and innovate in order to succeed. Unfortunately, many of us have forgotten how to delve into our raw creativity and leave behind the rigidity of the frameworks we have progressively interiorized.
This unique workshop seeks to reclaim our inspiration and imagination, rethink the unthinkable. It is ideal for people working in the creative arts as well as students, entrepreneurs, team managers, corporate leaders and anyone looking to implement their creative vision.

Inspiration is a vital driving force in our lives that moves us to create our best work and lights the way for new, authentic ideas. How do we invite, cultivate and harness inspiration so that we are able to bring these ideas into reality?
As a self-taught artist exploring various avenues of self-expression, Issa Sow draws a distinction between the phenomenon of inspiration itself and our task of making ourselves ready for it.
In the upcoming Inspiration Trap workshop, we will imagine ways we can invite and contain our inspiration, and well as keep our mind in the open, dynamic state as a receptacle or a “canvas” to collect, reflect and grow our ideas.
Feel free to bring along a personal object, a piece of clothing or even a small piece of furniture to play with during this hands-on experiment in innovative thinking. There are surprises and new elements in each session!

Issa =2
Issa Sow is a contemporary international autodidact artist known as Issa=2.
He believes in life being a journey of continual growth with each new

title: CANCELLED - African Dance for Beginners NEW
location: Montclair - Offsite, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.


	
		
			
			Join us for our all-new African Dance Workshop, an exciting opportunity to move, connect, and celebrate culture through rhythm and community. Led by Karen Miles of Zawadi African Dance and accompanied by two live drummers, this energizing class welcomes dancers of all levels.
			
		
	


The workshop begins with a 10-minute guided warm-up to prepare the body with rhythmic movement and grounding techniques. Participants will then learn Dansa, a vibrant traditional dance of the Malinké people from Upper Guinea.

Dansa is traditionally performed as a joyful celebration during community gatherings, often encouraging collective labor while strengthening unity and fostering a powerful spirit of togetherness. Experience the rich cultural traditions, dynamic rhythms, and uplifting communal energy that make West African dance so inspiring.

Note: This class takes place at DiRasa Gallery, 4 Lackawanna Plaza in Montclair.

title: PITCHAPALOOZA! with The Book Doctors
location: Mills Auditorium, 60 South Fullerton Ave, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
American Idol for books (only kinder and gentler) 
The Montclair Literary Festival invites you to Pitchapalooza, where writers will be selected at random to pitch their book. Each writer gets one minute—and only one minute! 
Arielle Eckstut and David Henry Sterry, co-founders of The Book Doctors, a company dedicated to helping authors get their books published, help you improve your pitch, not tell you how bad it is. 
Judges critique everything from idea to style to potential in the marketplace and much, much more. Authors come away with concrete advice as well as a greater understanding of the ins and outs of the publishing industry. 
Whether potential authors pitch themselves, or simply listen to trained professionals critique each presentation, Pitchapalooza is educational and entertaining for one and all.

title: & Sons at Luna Stage
location: Luna Stage Theatre Company, 555 Valley Road, West Orange, NJ, 07052, United States
description:
Winner of the Kirk Prize for Best New Play, & Sons by Jack Angelo Cummings is a sharply funny, quietly devastating portrait of brotherhood, labor, and the ways men learn—often badly—to love one another. 
On a New Jersey construction site, the DiSanti crew eats subs, burritos, and pizza on their lunch break while everything underneath begins to crack. Dom, the sweet-natured, perpetually high second son, is caught between his best friend Juan, a driven protégé hungry to lead the company, and his older brother Anthony, a imposing, tightly woundvfigure newly returned after years of unexplained absence. As power struggles escalate and old wounds resurface, the men avoid saying what they feel—touching, jostling, and posturing instead, using work and food as cover for grief, loyalty, and longing. By turns hilarious and aching, & Sons is an intimate meditation on masculinity, inheritance, and how blue-collar men translate emotion into action when language fails.

title: The Hardest Ideas in Judaism
description:
The Hardest Ideas in Judaism
with Rabbi Marc Katz
April 23, 30 and May 7 at 7:30pm 
Some of Judaism’s most powerful ideas are also its most challenging. In this three-part class, we’ll take an honest look at the concepts that many modern Jews struggle with—ideas that can inspire deep meaning for some but raise difficult questions for others. Together we’ll explore the notion of the Jewish people as “chosen,” the enduring problem of why good people suffer, and Judaism’s strong emphasis on Jewish community and distinctiveness in a universal world. Drawing on biblical texts, rabbinic sources, and modern thinkers, this class invites participants to wrestle openly with the parts of Judaism that can feel uncomfortable—and to consider why these ideas have remained so central to Jewish thought.

title: Bowling Night - North Jersey
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More (BVT)
This is an event for casual bowling at Montvale Lanes, 14 W. Grand Ave. All are welcome for **two games, food and drinks**, and any post- or pre-game hang out. Show up anytime! Questions or comments? You can message Andy Milone on Meetup, or call/text him at **201-234-9609**.

\*\*\* Before bowling, we might stop by the Pizza Parlour, 6 S. Kinderkamack Road in Montvale, for a few slices. Post a comment on the event page to gauge interest. **After bowling, we'll definitely be heading to Davey's Irish Pub & Restaurant, 5 Park St. in Montvale, or The Ridge Diner, 125 Kinderkamack Road in Park Ridge, at 10 p.m. for some food and/or drinks.** \*\*\*

About the group: People of all ages, backgrounds and abilities are welcome! We're not professionals and we're not in a league. In fact, we're a group of people who probably each won't score more than 100 points and will land more than our fair share of gutter balls. There's no pressure at all!!!! We're not here to analyze your form or technique.

More event details: You pay for your own games, food and drinks. Please bring cash. The alley does not accept card. But there is an ATM on site. **The** **cost per player is $18 for two games** **and bowling shoes.** If you have your own shoes, the cost is $12. Please try to bring exact change since Andy will have a limited amount of cash. If you bring a $20 bill and he doesn't have change, any remainder would just go toward the bowling alley tip.

Food and drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic) are available on site, plus tables and an alley bar to hang at during the event. There is a dart board and a few arcade games, as well.

**What do you do when you get there?** First, find the group inside around the front desk. Look for a growing group of people! Call or text Andy Milone at 201-234-9609 if you can't find us. Once Andy secures the lanes, please pay him before getting your bowling shoes.

**Please know that it is possible we have to wait 20-40 minutes until lane(s) free up.** It's also possible that we may have to relocate or cancel that night if there's a long wait list upon arrival. Please keep that in mind if traveling from far away!

For those who don't have cars or are looking to avoid driving, the Montvale Train Station is only like a five-minute walk from the bowling alley and can be reached via the Pascack Valley Line. Last train leaves at 12:20 a.m. and heads toward Hoboken. (https://gmtma.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/11/rail_system_map.jpg)

Many thanks to Taylor, one of our group participants, for recommending Montvale Lanes! You can learn more at: www.montvalelanes.com.

Hope you'll join us for our 23rd bowling event, or consider attending one of our volleyball, ping pong, skating or other activities -> www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball

If interested in staying touch with group members or conversing about future events, feel free to inquire about our WhatsApp group chat.

As we test this out, maybe this can be a staggered arrival event. So those who prefer later start-times can try and maintain momentum for the group and keep things going and courts reserved for those who are participating in-person with one another as through this group. If you are a serious attendee then please keep monitoring each event’s meetup app messages on your phone for updates for any one event you are seriously planning to attend.

There should be no formal teams (so we can fairly keep everything mixed) and everyone will essentially have to play both against and with everyone who shows up on any given day and time slot.

The goal should be for everyone to improve or maintain, but only within keeping positive group energy. Because the ultimate goal of course should be to socialize and have fun. title: Wissahickon Valley Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this diverse loop hike in the Wissahickon Valley featuring lots of different trails and such.
After meeting at the Acme in Flourtown, we will get on into part of Fort Washington State Park. We'll do all of the trails on the south side of the creek, then make our way onto some back streets and through ball fields south.
Heading south, we'll head into James A Cisco Park, then cover a few more back streets to Morris Arboretum. There is a charge for this section, I believe $10, walk in fee which is less than others. It should be a great time of year to see it, and so we'll spend more time there than we would have otherwise and try to do all of the trails possible.
After this visit, we'll make our way into the Fairmount Park sections view near connecting trails and meander through. This will lead us across the Wissahickon, and we'll then follow a circuitous route through the Andorra section, through woods and meadows.
After this, we make our way back to Forbidden Drive, and then follow the Green Ribbon Trail back to the starting point. A portion of that is along a back road, but there's plenty of grassy side to walk on that bit. The last stretch will be directly along the Wissahickon in a pleasant section.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

LEGO Robotics for Elementary Kids (Grades K–5) 
LEGO Robotics at Kinetic Minds introduces kids to engineering and beginner coding through hands-on building, testing, and problem-solving using LEGO robotics kits. 
In this small-group, drop-in friendly workshop, kids work in pairs to build real robots, program simple behaviors, and improve their designs through guided challenges. The focus is on curiosity, experimentation, and learning how things work—there’s no single “right” build and no step-by-step cookie-cutter instructions. 
Workshops are intentionally capped at a low student-to-instructor ratio to support collaboration, confidence, and meaningful learning. 
Kids will explore:
• Engineering and building with LEGO robotics components
• Beginner coding concepts (motors, sensors, cause and effect)
• Testing, debugging, and iterating designs
• Teamwork, communication, and explaining ideas 
Details:
• 60-minute session
• Small-group format
• No prior experience required

location: Luna Stage Theatre Company, 555 Valley Road, West Orange, NJ, 07052, United States
description:
Winner of the Kirk Prize for Best New Play, & Sons by Jack Angelo Cummings is a sharply funny, quietly devastating portrait of brotherhood, labor, and the ways men learn—often badly—to love one another. 
On a New Jersey construction site, the DiSanti crew eats subs, burritos, and pizza on their lunch break while everything underneath begins to crack. Dom, the sweet-natured, perpetually high second son, is caught between his best friend Juan, a driven protégé hungry to lead the company, and his older brother Anthony, a imposing, tightly woundvfigure newly returned after years of unexplained absence. As power struggles escalate and old wounds resurface, the men avoid saying what they feel—touching, jostling, and posturing instead, using work and food as cover for grief, loyalty, and longing. By turns hilarious and aching, & Sons is an intimate meditation on masculinity, inheritance, and how blue-collar men translate emotion into action when language fails.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More (BVT)
Because the early bird gets the tennis court! This time slot is a test-in-progress and feedback is highly encouraged! We can’t please everyone but maybe we can meet halfway and pass the torch along?

As we test this out, maybe this can be a staggered arrival event. So those who prefer later start-times can try and maintain momentum for the group and keep things going and courts reserved for those who are participating in-person with one another as through this group. If you are a serious attendee then please keep monitoring each event’s meetup app messages on your phone for updates for any one event you are seriously planning to attend.

For our early morning group I would like to throw in some quick-rotation points games (5-7 points and then everyone on that court do a 1-person rotation clockwise) maybe after some initial warm-up rallies if needed. There should be no formal teams (so we can fairly keep everything mixed) and everyone will essentially have to play both against and with everyone who shows up on any given day and time slot.

We are typically beginners to intermediate. If you are very good please go easier on less polished members while still trying to provide a bit of challenge for them. The goal should be for everyone to improve or maintain, but only within keeping positive group energy. Because the ultimate goal of course should be to socialize and have fun. And improving our game along the way is only the bonus!

DISCLAIMER: Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make serious plans to attend then please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you also agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety (e.g. you take breaks and hydrate at your own personal discretion, even if it has to be, for example, in the middle of a match). By attending you fully absolve anyone other than yourself for any liability regarding your own personal health at these events regardless of time, place, and weather.

UPDATE 1: Anyone who signs up is automatically signing up for being there at 8AM. If you plan on attending later then you need to comment here and tell us what time you'll arrive, most especially if you're running late the day of. Thanks for your understanding in the matter!

title: Spring Migration Special
location: NJ, United States
description:
Join David La Puma for this workshop where we’ll bird for everything on this three-day break, all things that make a spring week in Cape May so special. Celebrate spring with migrating songbirds and shorebirds teeming on the mudflats – Hooded and Yellow-throated Warblers sing in the shadows of Belleplain State Forest, while Summer Tanagers “piki-tuck” overhead; Red Knots and Sanderlings feed in mosaics of rust and silver along the Delaware Bayshore; assorted egrets and herons dot the saltmarsh and there’s always the chance of a lively fall of birds somewhere around Cape May Point. This workshop is all about the diversity of spring migration and focuses not just on identifying birds, but also on learning about their lives. This workshop will involve 1 evening birding session Monday night. The group will break mid-day, then reconvene around 7pm for dusk/evening birding. 
SPOTTING SCOPES ARE HIGHLY RECOMMENDED FOR THIS TRIP 
Because of the inherent dynamic nature of birding, we do not pre-set an exact itinerary but will visit those parts of Cape May County that regularly hold good numbers of birds. Final location decisions will be made by the leader based on local knowledge and conditions at the time. We will be walking several miles during this 3-day workshop, over generally level, sometimes muddy or sandy terrain.  
PREREGISTRATION REQUIRED – Ticket sales end 24hrs before start of program. 


COST: $250 members, $325 nonmembers. 
Interested in becoming a member? Please click on the following link to learn more or join: Become a Member today! 
IMPORTANT INFORMATION: 


We bird in all weather. Be sure to check the forecast in advance and dress in layers appropriate for prevailing weather conditions. The weather in Cape May can differ considerably from nearby inland areas and may be warmer, colder, or windier so it’s best to be over prepared. We may have to bird in the rain, so please bring your rain gear. 



TRANSPORTATION: Please arrive at the appointed time with a full tank of gas, as transportation to field sites is by private vehicles. We will be walking several miles during this 3-day workshop, over generally level, sometimes muddy or sandy terrain. 
CANCELLATION: CMBO programs require a minimum number of registrants to run, five days in advance of the start of the tour but are seldom cancelled. If we do cancel, due to lack of participation, severe weather, or unforeseen circumstances, we notify all participants in advance, and all are eligible for a full credit or refund. Participants may cancel without penalty if greater than 30 days in advance. Cancellations 10 to 30 days in advance may be subject to a 25% service charge. No refunds or credits for cancellations less than ten days in advance unless due to health emergencies 


REGISTER HERE

title: EARLY BOOK RELEASE: Christina Baker Kline ' The Foursome'
location: The Unitarian Universalist Congregation at Montclair, 67 Church Street, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
The Montclair Literary Festival and Montclair Public Library’s Open Book Open Mind present bestselling author Christina Baker Kline in conversation with her friend and colleague Alice Elliott Dark (Fellowship Point) about Kline’s new novel The Foursome. 
The Foursome is a boldly original reimagining of the astonishing true story of two sisters in nineteenth-century North Carolina — Kline’s own distant relatives — who married world-famous conjoined twins from Siam. 
Spanning five decades and unfolding against the backdrop of a fractured nation hurtling toward war, The Foursome is both intimate and epic. With piercing insight and emotional precision, Christina brings to life a forgotten chapter of American history. 
Tickets to hear Christina in person are $35 and include a signed copy of The Foursome. Christina will be signing books after the talk. 
The event will be held at the Unitarian Universalist Congregation at Montclair, 67 Church St, Montclair. Buy tickets here bit.ly/MLF-Four.

description:

Often called "the rainbow on the hill," Montclair's famous Presby Iris Gardens contain over 14,000 irises of approximately 3,000 varieties from all over the world and produce over 100,000 blooms over the course of the season. The Gardens were started in the 1920s as a memorial to Frank H. Presby, one of the founders of the American Iris Society and a Montclair local. Learn how the history of the Gardens at Presby entwines with the history of Montclair, its active citizens, and its early cultural scene. May is the perfect time of year to learn more about this unique park and to visit the irises in bloom.

title: Understanding Medicare
location: Montclair Main - Classroom
description:
Confused about Medicare? Join us for an informative session that breaks down the basics of this federal health insurance program. Learn who qualifies, including adults age 65 and older, younger individuals with disabilities, and those with End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD).

We’ll explain the different parts of Medicare—Part A (hospital insurance), Part B (medical insurance), and Part D (prescription drug coverage)—and what services each covers. The program will also explore your coverage options, including Original Medicare with supplemental (Medigap) plans and Medicare Advantage (Part C).

This session is ideal for anyone approaching Medicare eligibility, caregivers, or those looking to better understand their health coverage choices.

Presented by Medicare Specialist Jacki Spear.

title: Lunch With the Rabbi
description:
Join us for our monthly “Lunch with the Rabbi” class where each year a group of dedicated congregants meet and discuss a provocative Jewish book. This year we will be reading Rabbi Katz’s own Yochanan’s Gamble: Judaism’s Pragmatic Approach to Life. The book makes the claim that rather than have the intractable, strident discourse of today’s politics, we need to embrace the pragmatism of the Rabbis, which began with Yochanan ben Zakkai’s decision to trade Jerusalem of Yavneh. In essence, we can benefit today from the model of the ancient rabbis who make messy compromises, lead (but not too far ahead of their flock), change laws if they don’t work, and preserve peace within their community in order to better function in our day of division. 
Going forward, the class will meet monthly on the 2nd Tuesday of each month. Brown bag lunch (dairy or pareve) at 12pm, hybrid learning at 12:30pm. 
REGISTER HERE!

description:
Winner of CWA Dagger Award. A richly atmospheric, twisting "mystorical" set in Calcutta, 1919. The body of a senior official has been found in a filthy sewer, and a note left in his mouth warns the British to quit India, or else. Captain Sam Wyndham, former Scotland Yard detective, and Sergeant Banerjee, one of the few Indians to be recruited into the new CID—embark on an investigation that will take them from the mansions of British traders to the opium dens of the city. Perfect for AAPI Heritage Month! 

“An enthralling debut.”—The New York Times

Abir Mukherjee is the child of immigrants from India who grew up in Scotland. After 20 years of working as an accounted, he started writing crime fiction. "A Rising Man" is his debut novel. Mukherjee lives near London.

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: (CXLD) Wine Confidence 101: Understanding the Basics
location: Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

This introductory course offers a comprehensive overview of essential wine concepts, designed to establish or strengthen your foundational knowledge and support your ongoing appreciation of wine. 

Over the 5-week course, we will review the primary grape varieties and styles of dry white, rosé, red, and sparkling wines, as well as explore viticulture fundamentals and the winemaking process. We will explore the major wine-producing countries and differences among grape varieties and wine styles. We will review how to taste and critically evaluate wine from visual assessment through aftertaste. For historical context, the course provides an overview of wine’s origins, its evolution, and the business aspects of winemaking. A solid foundation also includes guidance on appropriate tools for opening wine bottles, optimal storage, and serving temperatures to enhance your overall wine experience. 

By the end of the 5-week class, you will have gained a deeper understanding of the many aspects of dry and sparkling wines so you are thoroughly conversant about wine and have tasted between 20 – 25 different wines from around the world!

title: Home Repair Essentials NEW
location: Montclair - Montclair High School, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register. 

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, Robert will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

title: Parent Academy Series School Year 2025-2026
description:
The Parent Academy is an engaging monthly program that runs September through June where parents and caregivers can learn practical tools and strategies to support their youth’s mental well-being. Each session focuses on a specific mental health topic and provides helpful resources and tips that can be used right away. 
These sessions are psychoeducational webinars, not to be used in place of clinical treatment. 
TOPICS: 
Suicide Prevention – Wednesday 9/17 12-1:00pm
Developed by the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention, the session is designed to help parents, teachers, and other caring adults recognize the warning signs of suicide in youth, initiate conversations around depression and suicidal thoughts, and guide them in helping young people access needed support and resources.  
Teen Dating Violence: Visible & Voiced – Tuesday 10/21 6:30-7:30pm
This session equips parents with the tools to recognize signs of dating violence in teens and respond with confidence. Learn how to spot red flags, support open communication, and help your teen build safe, healthy relationships.  
Less Stress, More Joy: Holiday Prep for Parents – Wednesday 11/12 12-1:00pm
This interactive webinar will help you plan for a more peaceful and meaningful holiday season. NJ4S will share simple strategies and practical tools to help you set healthy boundaries, manage stress, and prioritize your well-being.  
Spotting the Signs: A Guide to Youth Substance Use Awareness – Tuesday 12/9 12-1:00pm
PRESENTED BY Center for Prevention and Counseling
Participants will be equipped with tools and knowledge to recognize and respond to youth substance use.  
Suicide & Social Media – Wednesday 1/21 6:30-8:00pm
PRESENTED BY Jonathan Singer Ph.D., LCSW
This webinar will translate the most important research on social media and suicide risk into practical tips.  
Eating Disorders 101 – Tuesday 2/24 6:30-7:30pm
Information, signs to recognize, and resources will be shared on the topics of anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, and binge-eating disorders.  
High Stakes: The Rising Risk of Youth Gambling – Tuesday 3/10 12-1:00pm
PRESENTED BY New Bridge Services Information will be shared about the growing issue of youth gambling, shedding light on trends, what to look for, and available resources.  
Parent/Caregiver Support for Children on the Spectrum – Tuesday 4/21 6:30-7:30pm 
The session will provide a safe, supportive, and empowering space for parents/caregivers of children on the autism spectrum to connect, share topics, and build resilience through tools for mental health, self-care, and caregiving.  
A Parent’s Guide to Youth Mental Health – Wednesday 5/13 6:30-7:30pm
This webinar will focus on the various aspects of mental health, how to have the conversation with a youth in your life, and what to expect after the conversation.  
Bored to Brave: Building Independence through Community Adventures this Summer – Tuesday 6/2 12-1:00pm
This webinar will cover the impact of changing schedules, empowering youth to reduce screen time, and creating opportunities within the home, neighborhood, and community. Our NJ4S summer programs will be noted, as well as free resources within the counties.

During five episodes, we will see various responses to the unexplained. Whether they are controlled by superstition, are mishandling seemingly ordinary objects or dismissing what is not fully understood, each character must face the life-changing consequences
of their decisions.


Please join Linda Hetcher this season in the interactive study of the supernatural, most notably presented in The Twilight Zone.

title: Silent Failures in AI Data Systems: Risk Drift in Pipelines​
description:
Cloud Data Driven
As AI becomes embedded in cloud data platforms, organizations are encountering failure modes that differ fundamentally from traditional deterministic systems. In contrast to binary failures, AI-augmented pipelines often degrade silently, with quality erosion emerging gradually and compounding over time.

This talk explores key failure patterns in production AI data systems. Drawing from machine learning systems research, we examine how data and concept drift can persist undetected as models continue producing outputs despite shifting feature distributions. The risk intensifies in chained pipelines, where probabilistic errors compound across stages—for example, when upstream model inaccuracies propagate and amplify downstream.

We also analyze non-deterministic inference behavior, which complicates reproducibility, auditability, and root cause analysis in cloud environments. The session highlights risks of AI-generated data contamination, where synthetic outputs are mistakenly treated as ground truth, accelerating feedback loops and long-term model degradation.

At the infrastructure level, we discuss challenges such as non-linear inference cost scaling, observability gaps that mask semantic failures, and automation complacency that reduces human oversight.

The talk concludes with practical design principles for cloud data systems, including metadata-first architectures, explicit trust boundaries, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints to build resilient, auditable, and trustworthy AI-driven pipelines.

description:
Join us for a book talk with author Rae Dumont on her new novel "In the Shadow of Silence".

About the Book
Child psychiatrist Eva believes her lonely childhood gifted her with the intuition to connect with even the most troubled. When she meets Lyman, it seems that her dreams of having her own children are about to come true. They build a family. Their children grow up. But when Lyman abruptly stops therapy and medication, he spirals into a dark, irritable isolation that results in his suicide, leaving Eva to rebuild after his loss shatters her life.

Reviews
Editor's Pick: https://booklife.com/booklife-review/9798896360728
Readers Favorites: https://readersfavorite.com/book-review/in-the-shadow-of-silence

About the Author
Raymonde Dumont, MD, LMFT, is both a pediatrician and a family therapist. She practiced and taught for several years at Harvard Medical School, and at the Joslin Diabetes Center. She focused on the impact of one person's illness through their entire family, and also on the impact of mental health and family function on medical outcomes. 

She is currently a family therapist in private practice. She helps families to navigate difficulties by collaborating, rather than becoming divided. She is also a mother, a widow, and a friend to many. She lives and practices in Montclair, New Jersey, within reach of New York City.

title: Inspiration trap creativity workshop

Only 10 attendees allowed social distancing and mandatory mask wearing.

You are invited to participate in a special session of creative thinking and fresh insight dedicated to inspiration.

We live in a world of constant change that requires us to be able to continually adapt and innovate in order to succeed. Unfortunately, many of us have forgotten how to delve into our raw creativity and leave behind the rigidity of the frameworks we have progressively interiorized.
This unique workshop seeks to reclaim our inspiration and imagination, rethink the unthinkable. It is ideal for people working in the creative arts as well as students, entrepreneurs, team managers, corporate leaders and anyone looking to implement their creative vision.

Inspiration is a vital driving force in our lives that moves us to create our best work and lights the way for new, authentic ideas. How do we invite, cultivate and harness inspiration so that we are able to bring these ideas into reality?
As a self-taught artist exploring various avenues of self-expression, Issa Sow draws a distinction between the phenomenon of inspiration itself and our task of making ourselves ready for it.
In the upcoming Inspiration Trap workshop, we will imagine ways we can invite and contain our inspiration, and well as keep our mind in the open, dynamic state as a receptacle or a “canvas” to collect, reflect and grow our ideas.
Feel free to bring along a personal object, a piece of clothing or even a small piece of furniture to play with during this hands-on experiment in innovative thinking. There are surprises and new elements in each session!

description:

Marian Anderson was a celebrated American singer and a pivotal civil rights figure. Renowned for her rich voice, she broke racial barriers in classical music, famously singing at the Lincoln Memorial in 1939 after being denied a venue by the Daughters of the American Revolution. She was the first African American to perform at the Metropolitan Opera.

Join this class to prepare you for our outing, My Lord, What a Night!, a theatrical performance at the George Street Playhouse in New Brunswick on Sunday, May 17. An acclaimed play by Deborah Brevoort dramatizing the friendship between famed singer Marian Anderson and Albert Einstein, My Lord, What a Night! explores their response to racism after Anderson was denied a hotel room in Princeton, NJ, and Einstein hosted her, setting the stage for her historic civil rights activism.

description:

			Join us for our all-new African Dance Workshop, an exciting opportunity to move, connect, and celebrate culture through rhythm and community. Led by Karen Miles of Zawadi African Dance and accompanied by two live drummers, this energizing class welcomes dancers of all levels.
			
		
	


The workshop begins with a 10-minute guided warm-up to prepare the body with rhythmic movement and grounding techniques. Participants will then learn Dansa, a vibrant traditional dance of the Malinké people from Upper Guinea.

Dansa is traditionally performed as a joyful celebration during community gatherings, often encouraging collective labor while strengthening unity and fostering a powerful spirit of togetherness. Experience the rich cultural traditions, dynamic rhythms, and uplifting communal energy that make West African dance so inspiring.

title: Egypt: Beyond The Pyramids NEW
location: Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Most people picture Egypt as pyramids, pharaohs, and ancient temples. But Egypt is also the White Desert's surreal rock formations, salt lakes shimmering in Siwa Oasis, and valleys where whale fossils remain from a long-vanished sea. It's the unexpected green of Al-Azhar Park in the heart of Cairo, the ornate grandeur of a forgotten palace on the Nile, and the Bibliotheca Alexandrina, a modern landmark inspired by one of history’s most famous libraries. Whether you’re planning a trip or curious about Egypt beyond the usual sights, come discover a side that's often overlooked.

In this engaging talk, journalist and MSU professor Jenny Montasir, who lived and worked in Egypt for four years, offers a vivid look at both ancient landmarks and contemporary life. Whether you're a traveler, history enthusiast, or simply curious about Egyptian culture, this session brings Egypt to life through stories, visuals, and firsthand experience.

description:
Women’s Breakfast with “Farmher Leah” 
Rev. Leah, a.k.a. “Farmher Leah,” will be our presenter at the next Women’s Breakfast on Saturday, May 16 at 9:00 am. 
Rev. Leah believes that there is something holy and healing about putting your hands in the dirt – that growing food, feeding others, nurturing community, and caring for creation is sacred work. Her journey began in a single community garden plot in Oregon and grew into owning an urban farm in Detroit, Michigan, with years of soil, seeds, challenge and joy in between. Join us as Leah shares stories from her work as a farmer, food and faith educator, and food sovereignty activist. There will be a lot of pictures! 
Come on Saturday, May 16 to hear Leah’s fascinating story. A delicious breakfast will be served. Please RSVP to Karen Ermler, so that we can make sure we have enough food for this certain to be interesting event! 
Guests are always welcome. Hope to see you there!

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181

title: Forest Therapy Gentle Walk w/ Jojo ~1mi
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
A gentle, grounding Forest Therapy experience designed to help you slow down, connect with nature, and restore your senses. We will remain within a mile of our starting point at Tulip Springs, moving only short distances as needed for comfort and exploration.

This is not a long-distance hike, the focus is presence, noticing, and guided invitations that support relaxation and calm.

Welcome to bring something to sit on and a journal.

Due to the nature of this walk, no kids nor dogs. Just let me know if you'd like a family walk and we can schedule.

Meet at: Tulip Springs in the parking lot across the bridge

**Arrival: Please arrive 15 minutes before the start time for check‑in and settling in.**

Leader: Jojo Abenaavi Wright, cell # 973‑592-9062

This liability waiver and release extends to the SMC along with Essex County and its staff and any other affiliated organization or SMC partner. **BY REGISTERING FOR THIS HIKE I attest I am in good health and attest that I: Am not experiencing any symptoms of illness such as cough, shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, fever, chills, repeated shaking with chills, muscle pain, headache, sore throat, or new loss of taste or smell.**

Please come to the starting point 10 minutes ahead of time so the hike can start promptly. Times are our best estimates; they can vary depending on conditions, and the size and pace of a group. If you have any questions, call the leader. **Temperatures above 90 degrees and steady rain cancels, but intermittent drizzle does not. You will *not* be notified.** **Bring water. Wear hiking boots, preferably waterproof with good soles and traction devices and bring poles (optional).** Dogs are not allowed on hikes unless specified.
These hikes are publicized first to SMC members and then advertised to the public one week before a hike. title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

In this session, you’ll see demos and practical examples showcasing a wide range of enhancements, including:

Improved JSON handling
T‑SQL REST API integration
Expanded T‑SQL functionality, including fuzzy string matching and regular expression support
Time‑bound Extended Events
Change event streaming for real‑time data integration
Mirroring in Microsoft Fabric
Updates to change tracking and columnstore indexes

title: Inspiration trap creativity workshop
description:
Live African music and drumming events in NJ
6,7&8pm Issyra Gallery presents - Inspiration Trap Creativity workshop

Only 10 attendees allowed social distancing and mandatory mask wearing.

You are invited to participate in a special session of creative thinking and fresh insight dedicated to inspiration.

We live in a world of constant change that requires us to be able to continually adapt and innovate in order to succeed. Unfortunately, many of us have forgotten how to delve into our raw creativity and leave behind the rigidity of the frameworks we have progressively interiorized.
This unique workshop seeks to reclaim our inspiration and imagination, rethink the unthinkable. It is ideal for people working in the creative arts as well as students, entrepreneurs, team managers, corporate leaders and anyone looking to implement their creative vision.

Inspiration is a vital driving force in our lives that moves us to create our best work and lights the way for new, authentic ideas. How do we invite, cultivate and harness inspiration so that we are able to bring these ideas into reality?
As a self-taught artist exploring various avenues of self-expression, Issa Sow draws a distinction between the phenomenon of inspiration itself and our task of making ourselves ready for it.
In the upcoming Inspiration Trap workshop, we will imagine ways we can invite and contain our inspiration, and well as keep our mind in the open, dynamic state as a receptacle or a “canvas” to collect, reflect and grow our ideas.
Feel free to bring along a personal object, a piece of clothing or even a small piece of furniture to play with during this hands-on experiment in innovative thinking. There are surprises and new elements in each session!

Issa =2
Issa Sow is a contemporary international autodidact artist known as Issa=2.
He believes in life being a journey of continual growth with each new

location: UUCM-1-Mortenson (15) [Multiplatform]
description: The UUCM Council on Ministries (CoM) exists to report to UUCM, its Board and Co-Ministers on how our programs are accomplishing their particular mission while also furthering the broader mission of UUCM. Special attention is paid to any systemic or cultural obstacles hindering our ability to fulfill our mission as well as any conflicts. Its primary goals are to maintain UUCM's Mission & Vision, restore trust and relationship when frayed, and to keep all our interactions in line with UUCM's covenant. Join us in honor of **Citizen Science Month** as we explore different ways data is collected in SMR through our citizen science program. Feel free to join us for the entire tour or pop in for the program that interests you most. Ages 11+ (Adults are required to stay with their minors.)

Lori LaBorde, Citizen Science Program Coordinator, will be speaking about the history and trajectory of the projects and how these efforts benefit research and decision making at the local level.

**11:00-11:45am Meet at Shady Nook Parking Lot for a walkthrough of the Pollinator Meadow in its current phase. \*Please no bug spray.**

title: Meeting at the Verona inn!
description:
Board Game Night At Verona Inn
We will be doing our first monthly meeting starting on **February 25th at the Verona Inn!** We will be meeting up to organize games starting at 7:30, with food and drinks available courtesy of our host! You can play any game provided by hosts or bring your own! If you do not have a friend group to play games, hosts will organize you into pods with other people who need players. There are **no dues**. Future meetings will be held on the **last Wednesday of each month.**

More information and ground rules:

* **The doors open at 6:30 but games do not start until 7:30.** I *highly recommend* coming in during this period to eat your food and drink ahead of time!
* **Please return the graciousness provided by our hosts and order at least one item! All venue specific rules apply to our club.** Future meetings depend on treating our hosts with respect.
* **All games must be returned to their owners when they announce that they are leaving.** If you are in a game in progress when the meeting ends but it is not borrowed you may continue playing!
* **Please place food and drink on a separate table or surface from your games** to help avoid stains and other damage.
* **Please engage with others in good faith, sportsmanship, respect and common sense.** *ABSOLUTELY NO harassment, getting physical, hurtful insulting, and persecutory language will be tolerated.* Repeat violators of venue rules AND/OR this rule may be asked to leave the event and not return.

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: Centralized Data Lakes in the Cloud: Scalable and Governed Architectures
description:
Cloud Data Driven
Global data creation is projected to reach 175 zettabytes, with enterprises managing the majority of this growth. In data-intensive industries, organizations process an average of 9.1 petabytes per enterprise, exposing the limitations of traditional data warehouses. Yet 76% of organizations struggle with data lake governance, and 68% lack clear data ownership.

This session presents a research-backed framework for building centralized, cloud-based data lakes that deliver measurable improvements in performance, cost, and governance. Mature implementations achieve 3.2× faster time-to-insight, 54% reduction in data preparation effort, and 59.3% lower storage costs. Multi-layered architectures improve query performance by 73%, increase resource utilization by 81%, and reduce bottlenecks by 67.4%.

Cloud-native distributed storage supports 3.2× higher performance for mixed workloads, enables 8.7× more concurrent users, and delivers 99.99% availability. Beyond architecture, strong governance and master data management reduce inconsistencies by 83.6%, increase data utilization by 412%, and improve decision-making speed by 47.2%.

Security-by-design approaches reduce unauthorized access by 78.4%, lower breach likelihood by 56.2%, and decrease compliance penalties by 85.4%.

Attendees will gain practical, data-driven strategies to design scalable, secure, and governance-centric cloud data lakes.

title: Help Desk - Bring Your Laptop, Yourself, and Your WordPress Problems
description:
WordPress Montclair Meetup
If you are running a WordPress site and are having issues and would like some help, then this Meetup is for you!

If you know some things, expert or not, and want to give back to the WordPress community, then this Meetup is for you too!

We will do our best to match a problem with a problem-solver. On-site and in real-time. Just bring yourself, your laptop, and your WordPress problems.

It's OK if you attend and only want to observe. We recognize this is how people learn. Given our time limit of two hours, we may not be able to solve everyone's issues, but we will try! If you are seeking help, please come prepared. Have your web site loaded in a browser, have your WordPress admin ready, along with a short list of issues you are trying to solve.

People helping are volunteers and may not be experts. There is risk to breaking your site! Please do not bring client or business sites that can impact reputations or revenue. If you have a staging site we can test things with, that is always preferred. If it is a production site, please create a site backup before having someone do any work on your site.

If you cannot find the group, please ask the front desk where the WordPress meetup group is meeting.

**PARKING**:
We've been asked to not park in the United Way lot behind the library as it could result in a parking ticket. Please find street parking or a parking deck.

\-\-\-
Join the **JerseyPress Slack** group to chat with others in our community and get help: [https://jerseypress.org/slack/](https://jerseypress.org/slack/)

description:
**Midday MeetUp - Bonnie Rapp, Best of Broadway   
A monthly gathering to make connections and learn together.  
11:45am Catered Lunch (free)  
12:30pm Featured Program   
  
Experience *The Best of Broadway* as Bonnie Rapp brings to life unforgettable moments from Tony Award–winning musicals. Relive the golden age of musical theatre through beloved classics and timeless melodies by legendary composers such as Rodgers and Hammerstein, Lerner and Loewe, Frank Loesser, Irving Berlin and more!  
  
Cost:** FREE or Suggested Donation of $10 per person to offset costs. (Bill My Account is only open to Shomrei Members)  
  
**RSVP:** Required so we know how much food to buy.  
https://shomrei.easyshul.com/events/6967e6f2368f110026c0c486  
  
**\***Members & PreSchool Families should use their fob to access the building.  
 About Bonnie Rapp**  
Bonnie had the honor of performing the lead role of Christine Daaé in the National Tour/San Francisco Company of Andrew Lloyd Webber's The Phantom of the Opera. Some of Bonnie’s favorite roles include Maria in The Sound of Music, Kate in Kiss Me, Kate, Cinderella in Rodgers and Hammerstein’s Cinderella, Louise in Gypsy and Sister Amnesia and Sister Leo in Nunsense, Nunsense II and Nunsense Jamboree. In addition, Bonnie has appeared in numerous galas, fundraisers, and Broadway concerts, including performances at Lincoln Center's Avery Fisher Hall.  
  
For the past decade, Bonnie has devoted her talents to providing live musical entertainment for a wide range of audiences, including corporate and community events, libraries, private celebrations, JCCs, and residents of independent living, assisted living, nursing homes, and memory care communities.

title: NJ Code & Coffee - June meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

\*your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,

* What you can help others with,
\*What you would like help with,

title: South Mountain Crest Trail
description:
Let's Walk!!
Let's Walk!! in South Mountain and visit Washington Rock and traverse a few of the many trails in the Reservation.

Washington Rock is Essex County Park System's bona fide Revolutionary War historic site, dating back to the late 1700's when Beacon Signal Station 9 was located here—one of 23 beacons built by General Washington to observe British troop movements quartered on Staten Island and New York City.

Seems like a great place to remember the nation's 250th birthday

This hike will be about 3-3.5 miles and mostly flat. The terrain is mostly dirt trails in the woods, so please wear sturdy hiking boots. **Bug spray and protective clothing is a good idea.**

Please arrive a few minutes early. We start promptly at the time posted. The hike should take us 60-90 minutes. **Please remember to bring water!**

Inclement weather may cancel this event. Please check the event page for comments prior to leaving for the meetup.

**Disclaimer:** If you join this event, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap.

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**

title: 🥾 Let's Hike!! Jockey Hollow
description:
Let's Walk!!
Let's celebrate the nation's semiquincentennial (can you pronounce that?)

Come hike with us in the Morristown National Historic Park. We'll do about 3 miles along the Grand Parade loop, see a colonial era house and garden, and Revolutionary War soldier hut (replicas). It's a little like traveling back in time 250 years

[AllTrails: Grand Parade Loop](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/new-jersey/grand-parade-trail?u=i&sh=vgtzxk)

**PLEASE NOTE THIS WALK IS AT 09:30**
**Please arrive 5 minutes early so we can start on time.**

We've scouted these trails and find them appropriate for most of our members. If you've walked with us at Eagle Rock, this is similar in difficulty with just a little more up and down. There may be wet or muddy sections and a few rocks and tree roots. Please wear hiking boots/shoes and bring trekking poles or a walking stick, if you prefer.

Don't forget your water!

Inclement weather may cancel this event. Please check the event page for comments prior to leaving for the meetup.

**Disclaimer:** If you join this event, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap.

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181

title: Help Desk - Bring Your Laptop, Yourself, and Your WordPress Problems
description:
WordPress Montclair Meetup
If you are running a WordPress site and are having issues and would like some help, then this Meetup is for you!

If you know some things, expert or not, and want to give back to the WordPress community, then this Meetup is for you too!

We will do our best to match a problem with a problem-solver. On-site and in real-time. Just bring yourself, your laptop, and your WordPress problems.

It's OK if you attend and only want to observe. We recognize this is how people learn. Given our time limit of two hours, we may not be able to solve everyone's issues, but we will try! If you are seeking help, please come prepared. Have your web site loaded in a browser, have your WordPress admin ready, along with a short list of issues you are trying to solve.

People helping are volunteers and may not be experts. There is risk to breaking your site! Please do not bring client or business sites that can impact reputations or revenue. If you have a staging site we can test things with, that is always preferred. If it is a production site, please create a site backup before having someone do any work on your site.

If you cannot find the group, please ask the front desk where the WordPress meetup group is meeting.

**PARKING**:
We've been asked to not park in the United Way lot behind the library as it could result in a parking ticket. Please find street parking or a parking deck.

\-\-\-
Join the **JerseyPress Slack** group to chat with others in our community and get help: [https://jerseypress.org/slack/](https://jerseypress.org/slack/)

title: Meeting at the Verona inn!
description:
Board Game Night At Verona Inn
We will be doing our first monthly meeting starting on **February 25th at the Verona Inn!** We will be meeting up to organize games starting at 7:30, with food and drinks available courtesy of our host! You can play any game provided by hosts or bring your own! If you do not have a friend group to play games, hosts will organize you into pods with other people who need players. There are **no dues**. Future meetings will be held on the **last Wednesday of each month.**

More information and ground rules:

* **The doors open at 6:30 but games do not start until 7:30.** I *highly recommend* coming in during this period to eat your food and drink ahead of time!
* **Please return the graciousness provided by our hosts and order at least one item! All venue specific rules apply to our club.** Future meetings depend on treating our hosts with respect.
* **All games must be returned to their owners when they announce that they are leaving.** If you are in a game in progress when the meeting ends but it is not borrowed you may continue playing!
* **Please place food and drink on a separate table or surface from your games** to help avoid stains and other damage.
* **Please engage with others in good faith, sportsmanship, respect and common sense.** *ABSOLUTELY NO harassment, getting physical, hurtful insulting, and persecutory language will be tolerated.* Repeat violators of venue rules AND/OR this rule may be asked to leave the event and not return.
source: Meetup: Board Game Night at Verona Inn
